add_head: 🚀 **D-REFAV1-LAUNCHED — refav1 IS TRAINING ON THOR (PI decision 2026-09-02), AND THREE THINGS HAD TO BE FIXED FIRST THAT NO STATUS DOC KNEW ABOUT.** Run `/home/nvidia/experiments/refav1-b1-v72-1ep-21109`, supervised, target **21,109 steps = one epoch** — **168,873 windows ÷ bs 8, from the arm's OWN loader output**, not inherited (see D-ONE-EPOCH below, where the first figure was 4.8× wrong). **MEASURED 21.95 s/step steady-state at GPU 97–98 %** ⇒ **one epoch is 5.4 days of Thor.** ⛔ **The cost is COMPUTE, not data — my IO hypothesis was refuted by measurement:** 8 episode loads take **0.27 s at 1,865 MB/s** and the fp8→float32 cast **0.006 s**, i.e. ~0.3 s of a 22 s step; GPU sampled 97–98 % throughout. The arm predicts full **640×1024 patch fields at 10 tactical targets (0.6–6.0 s) plus 2 strategic**, which is where the time goes. **THE THREE FIXES:** ⭐ **(1) The v7.2 join existed at both ends and was not connected in the middle.** The loader had accepted `labels_path`/`nav_path` since 2026-09-01 and the model had masked `-100` correctly for longer, but `refa_v1_train.py` had **no `--labels` or `--nav` flag** — its own comment still said *"labels/nav join is the next increment"*. A run would have trained the trajectory path with the tactical and strategic heads **taking no gradient**, and it would not have looked wrong: losses fall, checkpoints land, nothing in the log says the hierarchy was never trained. Wired, plus a **refusal** (`--cache` without `--labels` exits; `--allow-unlabelled` is the deliberate override). Now MEASURED live: **labels 4,571/4,571 episodes (0 missing), 45,456/168,873 windows in-band ±2.0 s (26.9 %)**, nav 4,571/4,571, and `forward()` confirmed consuming `lat_label · lon_label · route_label · nav_cmd · str_ext_actions · str_ext_targets`. ⭐ **(2) A blind kwargs pass-through broke the moment the loader grew a field.** The trainer forwarded *every* batch key to `forward()`, which has no `**kwargs`; enabling labels made the loader emit `nav_valid` and the run died on `TypeError`. Now filtered against the model's **actual signature** (derived, never a hand-list that would drift) **and it reports what it dropped** — dropping a validity mask is correct, dropping a LABEL would narrow the run invisibly, so the reader is told which. ⛔⛔ **(3) ONE OF THE 4,713 fp8 PAYLOADS WAS TRUNCATED, AND A 12-SAMPLE CHECK COULD NOT HAVE FOUND IT.** `sha12:feec332cd22apt` is **61,624,320 B = 94.03 frames** — not a whole number, so truncated mid-frame — against a 96-frame minimum. The build reported *"ZERO skips"* and was content-verified on **12 of 4,713 samples**, which has ~2.5 % power to catch a single bad file; it was found only when the loader crashed on it. A full scan says **4,712/4,713 loadable, exactly 1 bad**. Excluded from the split. ⇒ **for a per-file defect, a sample is not a check — scan the whole set, and it is cheap** (mmap header read only). ⭐ **THE EVAL LEAK WAS ALSO REAL AND IS FIXED:** the fp8 cache is 4,572 train + **141 v7.2 EVAL clips** (0 unlabelled), the same leak refcv3 caught pre-launch. Symlink split built and content-verified: **train 4,571** (after the corrupt exclusion) **/ eval 141, intersection 0**. ⚠️ **A caveat that must travel with any refav1 route number:** `route_label` and `nav_cmd` derive from the **same `nav_command` field**, so on this nav-conditioned arm route accuracy measures the flagship-v1 echo (a bijection of its own input scored 1.0000), **not skill** — it is evidence only on a nav-shuffle control or a nav-less arm.
